facts.text: Ozone Park was one of Queens’ first planned suburban communities, featuring grid streets and easy rail access via the Long Island Rail Road’s Rockaway Branch.
When the Fulton Street elevated line opened in 1915, Ozone Park attracted a wave of Italian immigrants, reshaping its cultural landscape.
Cross Bay Boulevard, which opened to traffic in 1925, earned its name because houses there sit 30 feet below the surrounding ground level.
French immigrants Charles Lalance and Florian Grosjean founded a porcelain factory in the 1870s, built homes, and left only a clock tower after it closed in the 1960s.
St. Elizabeth’s RC Elementary and Divine Mercy Catholic Academy reflect Ozone Park’s strong Catholic heritage, serving generations of families.
Jack Kerouac lived in Ozone Park with his parents at 133‑01 Cross Bay Boulevard for eleven years after his discharge from the U.S. Army.
